records.public_claim_text: Unlike the original Logistics Performance Index (LPI), which was based on surveys of logistics profes sionals, the LPI 2.0 measure the speed, reliabil ity, and connectivity of supply chains based on observed shipment data.1 The LPI 2.0’s 21 indicators provide deep in sight into the functioning of logistics networks.

records.public_claim_text: Six core indicators (one connectivity indicator and one time indicator for maritime, air, and postal logistics) and 15 supplementary (connec tivity and time) indicators provide insights into maritime competition, transshipment burdens, corridor performance for landlocked developing countries (LLDCs), and postal logistics for e commerce.
